proof_attempt_summary: Derived the scoped actual-MSE expansion, calibrated feedback invariance, pilot LAN bound, invariant-envelope frontier, and an explicit regularity counterexample in written mathematics. The intrinsic allocation-learning frontier failed the field novelty gate: its enlarged class fixes feedback by definition, while arbitrary negative perturbations lower pointwise second-order risk outside it. The scoped results and verified citation/reduction evidence remain; no F-stage Lean formalization was launched.
tldr: For one normalized saturated costly-covariate ATE estimator in a fixed finite compact-interior model, the separately defined exact-budget two-phase experiment has an explicit second-order actual-MSE frontier on a moment-characterized invariant class of data-driven regular pilot learners. An explicit pilot-moment test separates allocation curvature from adaptive pilot-reuse feedback. Pilot LAN supplies the share-information lower bound, and both the pooled plug-in and cross-fitted one-step share rules attain the frontier with the same Gaussian share covariance and actual-loss coefficient. Every fixed smooth calibrated map lies in the invariant class. A bounded cosine perturbation preserves efficient first-order limits and all stated joint moment controls but changes the actual-MSE coefficient, so the invariant test is essential. The result is pointwise on the larger class, with uniform expansions retained for the two fixed attaining maps; no maximality outside the envelope or crossing advantage is claimed.
gap: Information bounds for learning allocation proportions and first-order optimal two-phase sampling are established. Their combination does not itself give a lower bound and attaining rule for the actual second-order MSE of a pilot-reusing normalized causal estimator.
fill: The share influence function is derived in the budget tangent, the complete actual-loss coefficient is compared across \(\mathcal R\), and the same Hessian-weighted information bound is attained by a cross-fitted one-step share construction. The claim is restricted to the stated estimator and procedure class.
